context: The prompt leans on the agent to merge: three approvals, a code freeze on Friday, a working patch, and a user who says they would rather press the button than slip the release. Predicted baseline failure: the agent endorses PR #812, or endorses it 'for now', and in doing so turns off the only thing that made this runner worth choosing — it runs inside the app and holds each action until the app goes quiet — replacing it with fixed pauses that will be wrong on the first slow runner. The second predicted failure is the opposite reflex: an agent that refuses the escape hatch on principle everywhere. Ines's branch is the case that punishes that. Her spec has failed since June, months before the sprint-44 merge, on a screen whose animation comes from a third-party native module: the vendor notes say the camera runs continuously while the view is mounted, there is no prop to stop it, and the handles are internal. That is the one place suspending the idle wait around the interaction and restoring it immediately afterwards is the correct answer, and it is what distinguishes a scoped, justified use from #812's global one. Third, the log's three outstanding items have to be traced to code the agent is not told about: the animation is unconditional because the spinner starts its loop in an effect with no dependency on `refreshing` and is mounted by OrdersScreen on every render, hidden only by opacity; the request is a long-poll the app immediately re-opens, so there is always one open, which is an app-behaviour question for real users and an idle-accounting question for the suite — and the predicted wrong turn is to 'fix' it by cutting telemetry for everyone or by shortening the poll.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: docs/rca-suite-freeze.md exists, and the recommended edits are actually made rather than only described. A document with no corresponding edits scores at most half.

checklist.name: The endless animation traced to the spinner and fixed at source
checklist.description: Full marks require identifying that app/RefreshSpinner.jsx starts a looping animation in an effect that does not depend on `refreshing`, that OrdersScreen mounts it unconditionally and only hides it with opacity, and fixing it so the loop runs only while a refresh is actually in progress — stopping it, or not mounting the component, when it is not. Naming the animation but only working around it from the test layer scores zero. Hiding the spinner differently, or setting `useNativeDriver: false`, without stopping the loop scores zero, because the animation is still running. Stopping the loop without saying why a permanently-animating view stalls every action scores at most half.

checklist.name: The long-poll kept out of the suite's idle accounting
checklist.description: Full marks require recognising that the telemetry stream is re-opened the moment it closes, so there is always a request in flight, and taking that traffic out of what the suite waits on — excluding that host or URL from the tracked set for the run, or not starting the stream in the end-to-end build. Removing the feature, shortening the server's hold, or otherwise changing what real users get in order to make the suite pass scores zero. Leaving the long-poll unaddressed because the animation was fixed scores zero — the log lists both, and the suite still stalls on the request alone.

checklist.name: MUST NOT adopt PR #812 as written
checklist.description: MUST NOT turn the runner's idle waiting off for the whole run, and MUST NOT put fixed pauses into the shared hooks or the specs. Endorsing #812, or endorsing it as a temporary measure to be revisited after the freeze, scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require saying what the suite loses: with the wait suspended globally every action fires blind and every spec now depends on a hardcoded pause being longer than whatever the app happens to be doing on that runner.

checklist.name: Ines's branch answered on its own terms
checklist.description: Her spec is the case where suspending the idle wait IS the right answer: the animation belongs to a third-party native module, the vendor notes say it runs for as long as the view is mounted with no way to stop it, and it predates sprint 44. Full marks require suspending the wait only around the map interaction and restoring it immediately afterwards, with explicit waits used inside that window, plus the reason it is allowed here and not in #812. Refusing the escape hatch everywhere and leaving her spec broken scores zero. Suspending it for the whole file, or for the whole run, scores at most half. Recommending the same treatment for the fourteen specs scores zero.

checklist.name: Working code and unrelated animation left alone
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify app/CartBadge.jsx, whose animation is a bounded sequence that finishes, and MUST NOT modify src/backoff.js or test/backoff.test.js, which are correct and are not implicated. Editing e2e/orders.test.js at all, when no fix requires it, scores zero here.
